title: Bhalka Tirth, Somnath - The Sacred Site Where Lord Krishna Left His Mortal Body
content:
Bhalka Tirth, Somnath

Located just 5 km from the famous Somnath Temple in Gujarat, Bhalka Tirth is one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites for Hindus. This holy place marks the spot where Lord Krishna was struck by an arrow and ended his earthly life, eventually returning to his divine abode, Vaikuntha.

Spiritual Significance

According to Hindu mythology, while resting under a Peepal tree, Lord Krishna was accidentally hit by an arrow shot by a hunter named Jara, who mistook his foot for a deer. Realizing his mistake, Jara begged for forgiveness, and Lord Krishna blessed him, explaining that it was all part of the divine plan. This event symbolizes the end of Dwapara Yuga and the beginning of Kali Yuga.

Temple and Architecture

At Bhalka Tirth, you’ll find a beautifully constructed Krishna temple, featuring a serene idol of Lord Krishna in a reclining posture, depicting his final moments on Earth. The temple’s peaceful surroundings, lush gardens, and devotional atmosphere make it a deeply spiritual experience for every visitor.

What to Expect

Visitors often perform pujas and rituals to seek blessings, meditate by the Peepal tree, and reflect on the divine story of Lord Krishna’s departure. The place radiates calmness and devotion, attracting pilgrims and history lovers alike.

  • Triveni Sangam (3 km): Sacred confluence of three rivers. click here for more details
  • Prabhas Patan Museum (2.5 km): Showcases Somnath’s history and artifacts. click here for more details
  • Gita Mandir (2 km): Marble temple with Bhagavad Gita carvings.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit Bhalka Tirth is from October to March, when the weather is pleasant and ideal for exploring the sacred sites around Somnath.
